archetype.name: Fringe Contender (shootout offense)
archetype.definition: A top-tier offense that lets Dallas outscore most of the league, tied to a bottom-tier defense that keeps the margin thin and leaves the record at the mercy of close games.

report.headline: An elite offense dragging the league's worst defense toward a playoff race
report.take:
Dallas is a one-sided team, and it has been for two seasons. The offense is among the league's best by any efficiency measure: 0.143 EPA per play (3rd), top-four through the air and on the ground, and a 50.7% success rate (4th). The defense is the worst in football by play-by-play EPA (32nd) and gives up the most third-down conversions in the league (48.3%). History says this is no fluke. The 2025 team had a 5th-ranked offense and a 32nd-ranked defense too, which is why it went 7-9-ish despite scoring plenty. The 2021-2023 Cowboys won 12 games a year because their defense ranked in the top four in EPA allowed, and that is what has gone missing.

The 5-6 record undersells the team a little. Dallas has outscored opponents 337-312, and the point differential implies 6.5 wins, not five. It sits 26th in wins over expected, and most of its losses came by one score: Baltimore by three, Arizona by three, San Francisco by six. That is partly bad luck and partly structural. A defense that can't get off the field on third down or keep teams out of the end zone in the red zone (67.6% TD rate, 25th) turns late leads into coin flips. Net EPA of 0.011 (17th) is the honest summary: league-average overall, built from two extremes.

The defensive numbers hide a specific shape. Opponents run against Dallas more than they should (pass rate 4 points under the norm, 29th), and the run defense ranks last in EPA allowed. The pass defense is decent against the deep ball (8th) but gets picked apart underneath (28th on short throws), and opposing No. 1 receivers have beaten their usual output by more than anyone in the league. The pass rush is getting home lately, with five sacks against Arizona, San Francisco and Tennessee, but the back seven is being held together with backups. DaRon Bland is on IR, both safeties Jalen Thompson and P.J. Locke are out, and linebacker Jaishawn Barham is out.

On offense, the line has kept Dak Prescott clean (3.8% sack rate, 5th), and the run game wins on success rate even though its 3.79 yards per carry is pedestrian. The ceiling is real: 40 against San Francisco and 51 against Tennessee in the last two weeks. The problem is the next month. After Philadelphia come Seattle, the Rams and Jacksonville, three top-six defenses, and those games will test whether this offense can carry a defense this bad against good opponents.

strengths.title: Top-three efficiency offense, both phases
strengths.body: Dallas moves the ball efficiently whether it throws or runs, ranking 4th in both pass and rush EPA. Prescott has started every game, and the target tree runs through CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens. The same profile held in 2025, so this is a durable trait rather than a hot streak.

strengths.title: Pass protection keeps Prescott upright
strengths.body: The line allows sacks on just 3.8% of dropbacks (5th) and few hits, even with an average time to throw. That protection lets the passing game stay on schedule. Guard Tyler Booker, a 94% snap starter, is out until early December, so the depth will be tested.

strengths.title: A run game that wins on success
strengths.body: Javonte Williams carries the load, and while yards per carry sit 19th, the run game ranks 8th in both EPA and success rate. It keeps the offense ahead of the chains rather than ripping off big gains. It also produced 204 yards against Philadelphia in October.

concerns.title: A defense that can't get off the field
concerns.body: Dallas allows the highest third-down conversion rate in the league and gives up touchdowns on two-thirds of red-zone trips. That is how a team that scores 30 a game keeps losing close ones. Last year's defense ranked 32nd as well, so this looks like a roster problem, not variance.

concerns.title: Soft against the run and underneath
concerns.body: Opponents lean on the ground against Dallas, and the run defense ranks last in EPA. The short passing game is nearly as bad, and opposing No. 1 receivers outperform their norms by more than against any other defense. These are the plays that sustain drives, which feeds the third-down problem.

concerns.title: A back seven built from backups
concerns.body: Starting corner DaRon Bland is on IR until late December, and safety Jalen Thompson is also on IR. Safety P.J. Locke and linebacker Jaishawn Barham are out, and linebacker Dee Winters is questionable. An already weak coverage unit is now thin as well, and it faces three strong offenses in December.

trend.note: The offense has heated up, scoring 30, 27, 40 and 51 over the last four games. The defense gave up 33 to Arizona and 46 to San Francisco in that stretch, so the results swing on whether the scoring keeps pace.

nextGame.headline: Thanksgiving rematch with a broken Eagles offense, Dallas heavy favorite
nextGame.body:
Dallas already handled Philadelphia 38-21 in October by running for 204 yards, and little about the Eagles suggests a different shape this time. Their offense ranks 30th in EPA, last in yards per game and last in success rate. Their line ranks last in stuff rate and 25th in sack rate. They have also started three quarterbacks: Jalen Hurts early, then Tanner McKee and Joe Milton III. Their defense is soft against the run (31st in rush EPA allowed), generates little pressure and has the fewest takeaways in the league. The Book makes Dallas an 8.5-point favorite with a 47.5 total. Both teams are on a short week, and Dallas has covered only 37.5% of the time.

Availability tilts toward Dallas but cuts both ways. The Cowboys are without Booker at guard, tight end Jake Ferguson, Barham and both safeties, with Winters questionable. Philadelphia is worse off: linebacker Zack Baun and receiver Dontayvion Wicks are on IR, and corner Quinyon Mitchell left his last game with a hamstring injury. McKee (ribs), Saquon Barkley (neck, illness), Will Shipley and Dallas Goedert are all questionable. If Barkley is limited, the Eagles lose the one way they could attack Dallas's worst unit.

waysToWin.title: Run through the Eagles' front again
waysToWin.body: Philadelphia's run defense ranks near the bottom by EPA, and with Baun on IR its linebacker group is thinner than in October. Dallas ran for 204 yards and 7.5 rush EPA in the first meeting. A steady Williams-led ground game also shortens the game for a Dallas defense that wants fewer snaps.

waysToWin.title: Feed Lamb against a shaky secondary
waysToWin.body: The Eagles allow 0.42 EPA per target to opposing No. 1 receivers (25th), and Mitchell's hamstring could take away their best corner. Their weak pass rush gives Prescott time even without Booker. Lamb's target volume lines up with the clearest coverage weakness on the other side.

waysToWin.title: Get early leads and pin back their ears
waysToWin.body: Philadelphia's offense ranks last in success rate, and its line gives up sacks at a high rate. If Dallas scores early, a backup-level quarterback situation is forced into obvious passing downs. That is where the Cowboys' recent five-sack games came from.

waysToLose.title: Third downs extend Eagle drives
waysToLose.body: Even a bad offense can stay on schedule against the league's worst third-down defense, especially one missing both starting safeties and a linebacker. Long drives would keep Prescott off the field and turn a mismatch into a one-score game. That is the script behind most of Dallas's losses.

waysToLose.title: Short-week sloppiness and giveaways
waysToLose.body: Dallas commits penalties at a bottom-seven rate and had 153 penalty yards at Indianapolis. The last time it played on four days' rest, it turned the ball over three times in a home loss to Tampa Bay as a 9.5-point favorite. Philadelphia can't take the ball away itself, so any turnovers would be gifts.

waysToLose.title: The run funnel finally pays Philly
waysToLose.body: Teams run on Dallas more than on almost anyone, and its run defense ranks last in EPA. If Barkley is healthy enough to handle a full load, Philadelphia's poor line still has a soft spot to lean on. Doing so would also keep the ball away from the Dallas offense.

nextGame.watch: Barkley's status and whether the Eagles can stay on the ground against the league's worst run defense; if they can't, this gets out of hand.

restOfSeason.body:
The offense is real and should stay productive, but the schedule turns hard after Thanksgiving. Seattle, the Rams and Jacksonville all rank in the top six in defensive EPA, so scoring will likely fall from its recent 40-plus peaks. The close-game record should drift toward neutral: a team with a 6.5-win point differential and five wins has been unlucky. Even so, a defense this bad on third downs will keep costing it late in games. Getting Bland back around the end of December would help, but probably too late for most of the hard stretch.

The path to the division runs through home games against the Giants in week 17 and Washington in week 18. Beating Philadelphia and splitting the next three would leave Dallas in that race. The likeliest outcome is a team around .500 that needs to win its last two division games, with the offense keeping it close and the defense deciding which way those games go.
swingFactors: Health of the secondary and Bland's return
Scoring against SEA, LA and JAX defenses

confidence.note: Eleven games, a profile that matches 2025, but heavy defensive injuries and a hard December.
